claims.statement: The Atlas reports a start estimate of about 410–375 BCE for Castell Henllys.
The Atlas reports an end estimate of about 380–190 BCE for this hillfort phase.
The Atlas describes evidence of metalworking and interprets Castell Henllys as probably supporting a wealthy farming community.
The map uses the Atlas site reference for Castell Henllys in Pembrokeshire.

evidence.note: Source summary gives no probability level. The estimate is retained without selecting a founding year.
This does not date all later activity: the Atlas also records Romano-British and later evidence.

evidence.locator: Summary, paragraph on radiocarbon dates and daily functions
evidence.note: The community interpretation remains qualified; individual activities are not assigned to 399 BCE.
Rounded coordinates identify the site, not its territory.
